system.biography: Barbarians and straggling demons left over from the Viper’s pogrom, the Burning Legions are led by self-proclaimed champions of this-or-that school or master of the fallen Five Stars. They bedevil the peaceful inhabitants of Heaven’s Wheel and surrounding lands, pillaging and raiding for food, fuel and slaves.
system.capabilities: Drilled and skilled in the use of their spears and shields. +1 Defense against all attacks due to their shieldwall tactics. Attack at reach with Spears.
system.tactics: Vanguard of powerful warlords, these elites form into a shield wall and march inexorably forward to engage foes with spears.

system.biography: The well-organized Silver Phoenix cultivate an equallyorganized and labyrinthine nemesis out of their political dissidents. Ultimately they pull the strings on them, but because this fact is never openly acknowleged, the rebels remain a useful tool for striking at one another’s political machinations.
system.capabilities: Highly-trained elites, serve as the surgical strike force of their distant masters. They hit high-priority targets hard then vanish. +1 Rank to all attacks and Armor 8 from their gear. Mastery of Senses and Agility due to advanced training.
system.tactics: Infiltrate, disperse or elminate low-value targets, then crush high-value targets with withering firepower.

system.biography: The well-organized Silver Phoenix cultivate an equallyorganized and labyrinthine nemesis out of their political dissidents. Ultimately they pull the strings on them, but because this fact is never openly acknowleged, the rebels remain a useful tool for striking at one another’s political machinations.
system.capabilities: None; they’re riled up out of radicalized citizenry. They’re just rioters, using whatever weaponry they have on hand.
system.tactics: Riot, loot, and cause mayhem in a chaotic mob. Easily discouraged; if they take any casualities, roll 1d10 at the end of the round and multiply it by ten. If this exceeds their current remaining membership, their nerve breaks and they split.

system.biography: Hollow-souled monsters, demons and vampires, led by the cruelest and most powerful of their kind. Their constant backstabbing and infighting is the only thing that keeps their raw power and unlimited numerical superiority in check.
system.capabilities: Gain 1 Prana per damage inflicted as a group. They unleash a Rank 5 blast of elemental energy on this Field and its enemy inhabitants for every 40 Prana eaten in this way.
system.tactics: Charge towards the nearest source of living Prana and devour it. Simple but effective! They don’t know fear and won’t stop fighting until utterly destroyed or commanded by a Sorcerer of impressive willpower (Degree 3+)

system.biography: The monstrous or sapient animal inhabitants of P’an-ku, united as a guerilla fighting force to repel the civilized man-apes they see as hostile invaders. Despise humans, but are somewhat envious of their technological capabilities and shrewd minds.
system.capabilities: Move at Speed 4. Because the animals fight as well as their mounts, they roll double the dice and have double the bonuses you would expect. Weapons grant +1 Rank to 4 attacks per round when they first charge into a fight and 1 attack per round therafter.
system.tactics: Sweep down from high places and scour through the ranks of their enemies. Fight doggedly, but if they get bogged down they gain Disadvantage as their lack of discipline catches up with them.

system.biography: The Scorpions produce many, many offspring and they cause loads of trouble. Disparate in ideology and circumstance, they share some common traits. Desert raiders and plunderers at their core, they’re not evil so much as they’re wild party animals with no plan beyond immediate and extreme gratification and damn the consequences.
system.capabilities: Keep a keen watch at Senses Rank 3 and obliterate anything that blunders into heavy machinegun range.
system.tactics: Purely defensive, these platoons hold down the fort while their brothers go out marauding (those lucky bastards!)

system.biography: The monstrous or sapient animal inhabitants of P’an-ku, united as a guerilla fighting force to repel the civilized man-apes they see as hostile invaders. Despise humans, but are somewhat envious of their technological capabilities and shrewd minds.
system.capabilities: Move through difficult jungle terrain with no hindrances due to magic and training. Weapons allow them to shot at range. Can use Art of the Priest using Platoon rules.
system.tactics: Guardians of sacred sites or elite archers, they use jungle terrain to their advantage to keep foes distant as they rain curses and arrows down on their heads.

system.biography: The politcal backlash of the Golden Lion’s strict governance is inevitably revolution. These attributes represent cells of free-thinking radicals, unified by ideology against those they perceive as tyrants. Make enthusiastic use of technology to give them an advantage over their supernatural swordweilding overlords.
system.capabilities: Highly drilled in stealth and reconnoitering. Equipment and training grants them +2 Ranks to all Senses actions.
system.tactics: Sneak into sensitive zones and gain information. Avoid fights where they can, but if they must fight, they strike hard from the shadows then scatter so that at least one of them can return to HQ and report.

system.tactics: Rely on overwhelming numbers and their natural speed to swiftly overwhelm enemies. They are ill disciplined, striking hard but quickly retreating if they encounter a stubborn resistance.

20 soldiers (counts as 60)

As the Cyber Thugs entry in the Bestiary (p. 193). Composed of one-third of the troops numerically one would expect due to their superior Ferocity. Run and climb at Rank 5, all attacks gain +1 Rank and deal +2d10 damage. Can fire a single burst of Ordnance per round raining a Rank 3 Fire Hazard on this or an adjacent Field, +1 Rank per 10 Thugs remaining.

system.history:
Grandfather of weapons and most ancient implement of war. Used primarily for defense, rather than attack. Sai and shield are also used in this manner.

Once per round, you may increase a defense by 1 Rank. For 3 Prana, you may increase another defense.

King of weapons and long considered the greatest strategic armament. Used by skilled combatants to control the flow of battle.

May attack into a neighboring Area. So long as you are engaged with a foe, you may use the reach and battlefield control offered by these weapons to increase your Initiative by 1d10. For 3 Prana, you may add an additional 1d10.

The preeminent weaponry of post-industrial advancement, these weapons barked death for centuries before magic dared to replace them. Includes semi automatic firearms of all varieties. These mighty weapons simultaneously act as Ranged and Balanced weapons, fusing the incredible killing power of the sword with the superior reach of the bow.

Once per turn, this allows you to increase a single attack, aimed at any visible target within this or an adjacent Field, by 1 Rank. Due to their mechanised nature, these weapons may not be imbued with magic to fire again.

Mustard gas, acid, or molotov cocktails douse the enemy in chemicals, burn them, or otherwise poison them. Rather than do damage they inflict their specified Hazard.

system.history:
Gentleman of weaponry; a vestige of an age which married civility and barbary. Perfectly honed killing instruments, they are coveted and feared by warriors.

With the comprehensive killing advantage offered by these deadly weapons, you may increase a single attack by 1 Rank once per round.You may channel this killing supremacy once again at the cost of 4 Prana.

Intellectual of all weapons, it is the mind’s grand art of killing made manifest. Also includes low-caliber guns, slings, boomerangs and other weapons used to strike at a distance.

Once per round, you may attack any visible target in this Field or any adjacent one, regardless of distance. Strikes utilizing this advantage consume appropriate ammunition: for a bow, an arrow; for a gun, a bullet. For 3 Prana, you may fire a second shot.

King of weapons and long considered the greatest strategic armament. Used by skilled combatants to control the flow of battle.

May attack into a neighboring Area. So long as you are engaged with a foe, you may use the reach and battlefield control offered by these weapons to increase your Initiative by 1d10. For 3 Prana, you may add an additional 1d10.

Tank-killers and regiment-annihilators, these weapons are powerful, destructive and cool as hell. Missile launchers, bazookas, machine guns, even flamethrowers are covered by this broad archetype. These weapons don’t require an attack and in fact, are operated like simple machines; point, pull the trigger, and unleash hell.

  • Unit-destroying weapons, like machine guns (Rank 4, Area) or flamethrowers (Rank 4, Fire Hazard, Area), have lower attack power but cover entire Areas at once.

  • Vehicle-destroying weapons hit once, but they hit hard. Rank 8+ is common. They hit with such kinetic force that anyone in the same Area as their impact suffers a shockwave effect at half the Rank of the primary attack (round up). Bazookas and primitive weapons are Rank 6 or 8, while missile-based anti-tank weapons can be Rank 10 or higher.

  • Ordnance weaponry generates enormous kinetic kickback when fired; they are therefore generally anchored to the ground or mounted onto a suitably massive vehicle, although a character who can brace against the inhuman shock can wield these weapons. It requires a sustained Power action of one Rank higher than lifting one of these elephantine weapons to brace against them when they fire and not be totally pulverized.

  • You must remain stationary in the round in which they fire.

  • Additionally, the ground beneath you must be capable of absorbing the kickback or you’re rammed through it as per being Thrown (p.11). Man-portable ordnance, like flamethrowers or bazookas, are designed to circumvent this problem. They therefore do not create any pushback. The above rule is instead for characters who lug around vulcan cannons (Rank 6, Area) and similar ludicrous armaments.

Once per round, increase a Grab by +1 Rank. This may be invoked on an already-extant grab to make it more difficult to escape. For 3 Prana, may empower a second grab.
